summary: Scott A. Mitchell works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008). He became a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and president/professor attested in 2026.

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After completing a doctorate at the Australian National University by 2011, he held posts at Hebrew University of Jerusalem, the University of Manchester (attested 2014), and ANU.

Sean D. Gaffney is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2003) under Tadeusz Skorupski, also studying under several other scholars, and held a post at SOAS (attested 1996).

Sebastian Nehrdich works in computational studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg (MA attested 2019 under multiple teachers), and served as a research fellow at Hamburg (attested 2024–2026).
Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related disciplines. He completed studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.
See Mui Yian is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Historian Seema Alavi earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge (~1987–1991). She taught at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1991–1994) and Delhi University (~1994–2008), before holding history professorships at Jamia Millia Islamia (~2008–2020) and Ashoka University (~2020).

Seigai Omura (1868–1927) worked in history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo Fine Arts School (~1889–1893) under Kanō Tomonobu, as well as under Umpei Shinma, and served there as assistant professor (1896) and professor (1905).

Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was an archaeologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Kosaku Hamada (~1925–1938; D.Litt. 1962), served as professor there (1949–1968), and held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture's Kyoto Institute.

Seiichi Yagi (born 1932) is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955). He held academic posts at Kanto Gakuin University (~1964–1968), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1968–1993), and Toin University of Yokohama (~1993–2002).

Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) studied law and philosophy at Tokyo Imperial University (~1914–1917, LLD 1933) under Eiichi Makino. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1922–1951) and later as professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

Seiji Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later held positions at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai (born 1980) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2004–2008) and later served there as an associate professor (~2013).

Seiji Nemoto (born 1949) specializes in history, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He completed his studies at Meiji University (~1968–1978) and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~1999–2014).
Seiji Tanaka (1897–1994) studied under Bruno Petzold. He later held academic posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1962–1976) and Asia University (~1976–1987).
Seijun Ishii (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1977–1986) and later served there as a professor (~1999).

Seikaku Hirata (1924–2008) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki, and held a post at Hanazono University (~1957–1995).

Seiki Kudo (born 1931) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held academic appointments as an assistant at Kyoto University and as an associate professor at Shuchiin University and Shitennoji University (~1970).
Sein Tin (1899–1942) was a Burmese scholar and linguist. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1918–1923), under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927), and at Christ Church, University of Oxford (~1927–1930).
Seiran Ouchi (1845–1918) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served in an advisory post (jiko) at Nishi Hongan-ji and served as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.
